learn.hook: Your shadow follows you everywhere, but it is short at noon and super-long in the evening. Why does it keep changing size?
points: Light travels in a straight line. That is why we cannot see around a corner.

Transparent materials (clear glass, clean water) let almost all light through. Translucent ones (butter paper, frosted glass) let some light through. Opaque ones (wood, cardboard, your body) let no light through.
A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light. We need a light source, an opaque object and a surface (screen) to see a shadow.
A shadow is dark whatever the colour of the object. Its size depends on how near the object is to the light: closer to the light gives a bigger shadow.
A pinhole camera shows that light travels in straight lines: the image it forms on its screen is upside down.

example.q: During shadow-puppet play, Arjun moves his hand closer to the torch. What happens to the shadow on the wall?
steps: The torch spreads light outwards in straight lines.
When the hand is closer to the torch, it blocks a wider part of the spreading light.
So a bigger area of the wall gets no light.

learn.reallife: Shadow puppetry, like Tholu Bommalata of Andhra Pradesh and Togalu Gombeyaata of Karnataka, uses light and shadows to tell stories.

games.title: Shadow facts
items: A red ball makes a red shadow.
A shadow is just an area where light is blocked, so it is dark whatever the object's colour.
Light travels in a straight line.
That is why shadows have sharp shapes and we cannot see around corners.
Our shadows are shortest around noon.
The Sun is highest in the sky around noon, so shadows are short.
A pinhole camera forms an upside-down image.
Light rays from the top and bottom cross at the pinhole, so the image is inverted.
Transparent objects make dark shadows.
Transparent objects let light through, so they do not make dark shadows.

quiz.q: A shadow is formed when light is blocked by:
quiz.explain: Opaque objects do not let light pass, so a dark region forms behind them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks transparent objects make shadows

quiz.q: Which of these is translucent?
quiz.explain: Butter paper lets some light through but you cannot see clearly through it.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up translucent and transparent

quiz.q: What colour is the shadow of a green leaf in sunlight?
quiz.explain: A shadow is a region where light does not reach, so it is dark no matter the colour of the object.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a shadow takes the colour of the object

quiz.q: What does a pinhole camera show about light?
quiz.explain: Straight rays crossing at the pinhole make an upside-down image, which proves light travels straight.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the inverted image with straight-line travel

quiz.q: The image of a tree in a pinhole camera is:
quiz.explain: Rays from the top of the tree go down through the hole and rays from the bottom go up, so the image is inverted.
quiz.mistake: Expects the image to be upright like a photo

quiz.q: When are our shadows the longest on a sunny day?
options: They are always the same length
quiz.explain: When the Sun is low in the sky, shadows stretch out long.
quiz.mistake: Thinks shadows are longest when the Sun is highest

quiz.q: Which three things are needed to see a shadow?
options: A light source, an opaque object and a screen
quiz.explain: Light must be blocked by an opaque object and fall on a surface for the shadow to be seen.
quiz.mistake: Forgets one of the needed parts

quiz.q: Why can't you see a friend hiding around the corner of a wall?
options: Light travels in straight lines and cannot bend around the wall
quiz.explain: Light from your friend would have to bend around the corner to reach your eyes, but it travels straight.
quiz.mistake: Does not apply straight-line travel of light

teach.ask: Gappu sees a funny long shadow following it in the evening. Why do shadows form and why do they change?
teach.praise: Chirp! Opaque things block light that travels in straight lines, and that makes shadows. Gappu loves shadow play!
teach.nudge: What kind of object blocks light to make a shadow?

learn.hook: You can see this page only because light bounces off it into your eyes. That bounce has a name!
points: Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it falls on a surface. Smooth, shiny surfaces like mirrors reflect light very well.
The ray that falls on the mirror is the incident ray; the ray that bounces off is the reflected ray. The normal is an imaginary line at 90° to the mirror at the point where the ray hits.
The angle of incidence is the angle between the incident ray and the normal. The angle of reflection is the angle between the reflected ray and the normal.
Law 1: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
Law 2: the incident ray, the normal and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane (on the same flat surface).

example.q: A ray of light hits a plane mirror making an angle of 30° with the mirror's surface. What are the angles of incidence and reflection?
steps: The normal is at 90° to the mirror.
Angle of incidence = 90° − 30° = 60° (measured from the normal, not the mirror).
Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 60°.

learn.reallife: Bicycles have reflectors that shine when car lights fall on them at night, and road signs are made with reflective paint for safety.

quiz.q: What is reflection of light?
options: Light being made by a bulb
The bouncing back of light from a surface
quiz.explain: When light hits a surface and bounces back, it is reflected.
quiz.mistake: Confuses reflection with light passing through

quiz.q: The angle of incidence is 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
quiz.explain: By the first law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 90° or doubles the angle

quiz.q: A ray of light strikes a mirror making 50° with the mirror's surface. What is the angle of incidence?
quiz.explain: Angles are measured from the normal. 90° − 50° = 40°.
steps: Normal is at 90° to the mirror
quiz.mistake: Measures the angle from the mirror instead of the normal

quiz.q: The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is 80°. What is the angle of incidence?
quiz.explain: The normal splits the 80° equally, because both angles are equal: 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.
steps: They are equal, so each is 80 ÷ 2 = 40°
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the angle between the rays is the sum of the two equal angles

quiz.q: What is the normal in reflection?
options: A line at 90° to the mirror at the point where light hits
quiz.explain: The normal is drawn perpendicular to the mirror. Angles of incidence and reflection are measured from it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the normal is the mirror line

quiz.q: A ray of light falls on a mirror along the normal. In which direction does it reflect?
options: Straight back along the same path
quiz.explain: The angle of incidence is 0°, so the angle of reflection is also 0°: the ray goes straight back.
quiz.mistake: Does not apply the law of reflection to a 0° angle

quiz.q: Which surface reflects light best to form clear images?
quiz.explain: Smooth, shiny surfaces reflect light regularly, so clear images form.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all surfaces reflect equally

quiz.q: Why is it dangerous to reflect sunlight into someone's eyes with a mirror?
options: Strong reflected sunlight can damage the eyes
quiz.explain: Sunlight is very bright. Reflecting it into eyes can harm them, so never do it.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about eye safety

teach.ask: Gappu shone a torch at a mirror and the light bounced to a different spot! What rule does the bouncing light follow?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Gappu is a light-bouncing expert!
teach.nudge: How are the angle of incidence and angle of reflection related?

learn.hook: Why is the word AMBULANCE written backwards on the front of ambulances? Look in a mirror and find out!
points: A plane (flat) mirror forms an image that is upright (erect) and the same size as the object.
The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it.
The image is laterally inverted: left and right appear swapped. Your right hand looks like the image's left hand.
The image in a plane mirror cannot be caught on a screen; it is a virtual image.

Curved mirrors: a concave mirror curves inwards (like the inside of a steel spoon) and is used by dentists and in torch reflectors. A convex mirror bulges outwards and gives a wider view, so it is used as the side mirror on vehicles.

example.q: Priya stands 3 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is she from her image?
steps: Her image is as far behind the mirror as she is in front: 3 m.
Distance from Priya to the image = 3 m + 3 m.

learn.reallife: Periscopes use two plane mirrors to see over walls, kaleidoscopes use mirror strips to make patterns, and convex mirrors are placed at sharp mountain-road bends to show oncoming traffic.

games.title: Plane mirror image check
items: The image in a plane mirror is the same size as the object.
A plane mirror neither enlarges nor shrinks the image.
The image in a plane mirror is upside down.
It is upright, but left and right are swapped.
If you raise your right hand, your image seems to raise its left hand.
This is lateral inversion.
A plane mirror image can be caught on a screen.
It is a virtual image, so it cannot be formed on a screen.
Side mirrors of vehicles are convex because they show a wider area.
A convex mirror gives a smaller image but covers a bigger field of view.

quiz.q: Which of these describes the image in a plane mirror?
quiz.explain: A plane mirror gives an erect image of the same size as the object.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up plane-mirror images with curved-mirror images

quiz.q: Rohan stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is his image from him?
quiz.explain: The image is 2 m behind the mirror, so it is 2 + 2 = 4 m from Rohan.
steps: Image is 2 m behind the mirror
quiz.mistake: Gives only the distance from the mirror

quiz.q: Why is 'AMBULANCE' written in mirror letters on the front of the vehicle?
options: So drivers ahead can read it correctly in their mirrors
So it can be read only from inside
quiz.explain: A plane mirror swaps left and right, so the reversed word appears correct in the rear-view mirror.
quiz.mistake: Does not apply lateral inversion

quiz.q: Swapping of left and right in a mirror image is called:
quiz.explain: Lateral means sideways. The image is inverted from side to side.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the term

quiz.q: Which mirror is used as the side mirror of vehicles because it shows a wider area?
quiz.explain: Convex mirrors give a wider view of the traffic behind.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up concave and convex mirrors

quiz.q: Dentists use which mirror to see an enlarged image of teeth?
quiz.explain: A concave mirror held close to the teeth gives an enlarged, upright image.
quiz.mistake: Thinks convex mirrors magnify

quiz.q: The inner (hollow) side of a shiny steel spoon behaves like a:
quiz.explain: The inner side curves inwards like a cave, which makes it concave.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the inner and outer sides of a spoon

quiz.q: A periscope helps you see over a wall. What does it use?
quiz.explain: Two plane mirrors, fixed at 45°, reflect light down the tube to your eye.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how a periscope works

teach.ask: Gappu looked in a mirror and saw a Gappu waving with the other wing! What is special about a mirror image?
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Same size, upright, same distance behind, and left-right swapped. Gappu waves at Gappu!
teach.nudge: What happens to left and right in a mirror image?
